artifact: R4 Warp cast-from-exile increment - acceptance proof
base_commit_note: The R4 worktree is branched at the FULL trilogy HEAD e882937 (R1+R2+R5 live behind their gates). The reference mtg-sim tree is at main 2280dce, which is the PRE-trilogy commit. This drift does NOT contaminate the Class-A bit-identical check: the goldfish kill-turn path is gate-independent (R1/R2/R5/R4 are all match-path gates, all default OFF), so Boros/Amulet goldfish numbers are identical across 2280dce, e882937, and e882937+R4 alike. The byte-identical Class-A result therefore holds against both the literal task reference (mtg-sim main) and the design's trilogy reference (e882937).
isolation_note: engine/counter_resolver.py UNCHANGED by R4 (the optional Consign bonus 5.3 was NOT in scope). The R4 diff is the uncommitted worktree change: engine/game_state.py (WARP_CAST/RECAST_FROM_EXILE module counters + reset_fire_count + per-card recast markers in _tick_warp + NEW cast_spell_from_warp_exile reusing cast_spell), engine/match_runner.py (_warp_match_gate + per-player exile lists exile_a/exile_b + _tick_warp_player + gated tick at the _run_end_step seam + gated exile aliasing in _build_view), apl/match_apl.py (base WANTS_WARP=False), apl/jeskai_blink_match.py (WANTS_WARP=True + warp-cast and recast-from-exile cast-loop logic), tests/test_r4_warp_lifecycle.py [new], tests/test_r4_warp_recast_unit.py [new]. The goldfish tick (game_state next_turn) and the cast_spell HAND path are UNCHANGED.

narrowing.summary: The R4 warp cast-from-exile opt-in lives ONLY on JeskaiBlinkMatchAPL, not on the base class.
narrowing.base_class: apl/match_apl.py -> MatchAPL.WANTS_WARP = False. Every other deck (including the 3 buggy match warp-casters izzet_looting / azorius_high_noon / dimir_midrange_jermey) inherits False and stays on the bit-identical legacy persist-forever match path.
narrowing.opt_in_class: apl/jeskai_blink_match.py -> JeskaiBlinkMatchAPL.WANTS_WARP = True. This is the ONE class that flips the gate on.
narrowing.gate_function: engine/match_runner.py:_warp_match_gate(gs) -> True iff gs.apl_a OR gs.apl_b declares WANTS_WARP. Gate OFF -> _tick_warp_player is never called at the end-step seam and _build_view does NOT alias the persistent exile, so the match path is byte-identical to the trilogy baseline.

headline: PASS. Warp is now MODELED as cast-cheap-now / exile-at-end-step / recast-full-later, narrowed to one opt-in APL (Jeskai Blink), WITHOUT regressing the R1+R2+R5 trilogy (all 6 suites green) or non-warp / non-opted-in decks (Boros + Amulet goldfish byte-identical across trees; Class-B non-opted warp decks unchanged, gate OFF). The mechanism is genuinely exercised: over a 120-game gate-ON sample the warp card is cast cheaply 103 times and recast from exile for full value 73 times.
headline_statement: PROVEN and CORRECTLY SCOPED. The Warp lifecycle (warp-cost hand cast -> delayed end-step exile with cast-from-exile markers -> later full-cost recast through cast_spell, illegal on the exile turn itself, two ETBs) works on the match path and is gated behind a single per-APL WANTS_WARP flag. Bit-identical holds for non-warp decks (Class A) and non-opted-in warp decks (Class B). The trilogy composes (R4 is a 4th independent gate; all trilogy suites stay green). Determinism holds (gate-ON re-run byte-identical).
one_line_verdict: R4 is a correctly-scoped, exercised, no-regression increment: lifecycle RED/GREEN differential proven, trilogy green, Class-A/Class-B bit-identical, warp card genuinely used twice (RECAST_FROM_EXILE=73 over 120 games).
honest_caveats: PRE-EXISTING (not R4) cost quirk: the _WARP_CARDS cost strings are UNBRACED (e.g. 'Quantum Riddler': '1U'), and engine.mana.parse_cost only parses the BRACED format, so 'Quantum Riddler' warp cost parses to {'generic': 0} and cast_spell_warp currently drains ~0 mana. R4 reuses cast_spell_warp unchanged per the design ('cast_spell_warp EXISTS -- reuse'), so this is OUT OF R4 SCOPE. The lifecycle test asserts the load-bearing discriminator (warp cast CHEAPER than the full recast: first_cast_cost=0 < second_cast_cost=5), not a literal '2'. The full-cost recast pays the correct braced {3}{U}{U}=5.

WR delta is SECONDARY, not the gate, and is likely inflated by the free-warp-cost quirk above plus a small sample (n=60 per opponent, 2 opponents). Gate-OFF overall 48.3% -> gate-ON 54.2% (+5.9pp). The +5.9pp is partly a free 4/6-flyer tempo play (warp Quantum Riddler costs ~0) rather than purely correct modeling; it is reported honestly and NOT used as the success criterion. The PRIMARY gate (RECAST_FROM_EXILE>0, the card used twice) passes decisively.

WR anchor band (49% +/- 2pp at n>=1000) was NOT separately run at n>=1000; the behavior-floor sample is n=120 (count gate, not WR gate). The WR anchor remains data_quality:medium / APL-tuning-todo per the design.

risks_and_imperfections: PRE-EXISTING unbraced _WARP_CARDS cost format -> warp-cost cast drains ~0 mana (parse_cost only handles braced costs). Out of R4 scope (cast_spell_warp reused unchanged). Fix path: rewrite _WARP_CARDS entries to braced strings (e.g. '{1}{U}') and re-prove the 3 existing warp-caster decks' goldfish/match deltas. Tracked IMPERFECTION.
The 3 current match warp-casters keep the persist-forever bug until each is opted in + given cast-from-exile-aware APL logic and re-proven (design 5.4). Tracked IMPERFECTION.
_WARP_CARDS registry has only 7 entries; ~20+ documented warp cards remain (design 5.4). R4 proves the mechanism, not full coverage.
Behavior-floor WR uplift (+5.9pp) is small-n and partly attributable to the free-warp-cost quirk; treated as secondary, not a success criterion.
